title: A Mixtape for the Semester
premise: Juniper Okonkwo has survived three years at tiny Millbrook High by being careful: invisible, unremarkable, safe. Then English teacher Ms. Voss pairs him with Theo Brandt — star wrestler, son of the pastor who led the town's fight against the school's GSA — for a semester project building an oral history of the town, set to a shared mixtape. As forced proximity becomes real friendship and then something neither can name, Juniper must choose between protecting his secret and telling the truth that could cost him Theo, his last semester, and any hope of belonging. The story ends with Juniper broadcasting their mixtape over the school radio during the state championship, claiming his voice publicly; Theo chooses him in front of the whole town, and they lose the match but win everything that matters.
about_author: Edmund Joubert is the pen name of a former small-town radio DJ who grew up as one of four out teenagers in a farming county of eleven thousand people. He writes tender, music-soaked stories about kids who learn that being seen is worth the risk.

chapters.title: The Careful Boy
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A ordinary Monday establishes his survival rules: sit near exits, laugh at the right jokes, never correct anyone about Danny Reyes from two summers ago. The emotional beat is exhaustion disguised as calm — we feel how much energy invisibility costs.

chapters.title: Assigned Seating
chapters.summary: Ms. Voss announces the semester project: pairs will build a town oral history with a companion mixtape. Juniper draws Theo Brandt, who once held his backpack over a toilet in freshman year. Theo's POV reveals he volunteered for the project to escape his father's expectations. Beat: mutual dread.

chapters.title: Ground Rules
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The boys negotiate truce terms in the library: no personal questions, work only at school, finished by May. Juniper notices Theo flinch when his father texts. Beat: wary professionalism masking curiosity on both sides.

chapters.title: Mrs. Ellery's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. First interview subject: the retired music teacher who remembers every student since 1974. She plays them a cassette she made for her late wife, casually, decades ago. Juniper goes very still. Beat: the first crack in both boys' certainties about each other.

chapters.title: Track Three
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. He adds a song to the shared mixtape without explanation — something raw he'd never play aloud. Theo doesn't ask, but listens to it eleven times that night. Beat: music becoming a language before words are safe.

chapters.title: Wrestling Season
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Juniper shows up to film the team for the project and watches Theo win, seeing him fully for the first time. Teammates' casual slurs land differently now that Theo hears them through Juniper's silence. Beat: guilt and unwanted tenderness.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Trapped late in the basement archive by a storm, they find photos of the town's 1989 prom — including two boys holding hands, faces half-turned away. Neither comments. Beat: history offering permission neither boy can accept yet.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Working in Theo's truck after practice, close in the cab, a moment almost happens — interrupted by Pastor Brandt pulling into the church lot across the street. Theo goes rigid. Beat: desire colliding with fear, the first time Juniper sees Theo's cage.

chapters.title: What Danny Knew
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Juniper finally tells Theo about Danny Reyes — the boy who left town after they were caught, and what it did to Juniper's family. Theo listens without flinching. Beat: trust deepening; Theo realizes his father was part of that exodus.

chapters.title: State Qualifiers
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo qualifies for the state wrestling championship, fulfilling his father's dream. The celebration dinner feels like a sentencing. Juniper films it all, invisible again, and hates it. Beat: success as trap; the championship that 'doesn't matter' takes shape.

chapters.title: Side B
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper flips the mixtape to Side B and writes a note inside the case: 'Ask me.' Theo reads it in class and says nothing, but his knee presses against Juniper's under the desk for the entire period. Beat: the question asked without asking.

chapters.title: The Water Tower
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They climb the water tower at night to record the town soundscape. At the top, Theo kisses him. It lasts nine seconds before Theo pulls back, terrified, and drives home in silence. Beat: euphoria curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Radio Silence
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Four days of nothing. Juniper drafts and deletes forty messages, reliving Danny all over again. Ms. Voss, sensing trouble, quietly tells Juniper the project grade is already secured — he can walk away. Beat: old wounds insisting they were right.

chapters.title: Confession
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confesses to his youth group leader instead of to Juniper, hoping for absolution. Instead, word reaches his father. The confrontation at home is quiet and devastating: choose the family or choose 'that life.' Beat: love against duty made literal.

chapters.title: The Sermon
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Pastor Brandt preaches on Sunday about 'loving the sinner,' eyes finding Juniper's family in the third pew. Half the congregation won't meet his mother's gaze afterward. Beat: public humiliation; the town closing ranks exactly as Juniper predicted.

chapters.title: Burned
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo returns Juniper's mixtape, case cracked, and asks him to deny it happened — just until after states, just until graduation. Juniper refuses to be anyone's secret twice. Beat: the breakup that isn't a breakup; loyalty vs. truth splitting them apart.

chapters.title: Empty Tracks
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper finishes the oral history alone, interviewing Mrs. Ellery one last time. She tells him about the 1989 boys: one stayed and married, one left and never called, and both regretted it. 'The tape doesn't care who's listening,' she says. Beat: wisdom arriving too late to be comfortable.

chapters.title: Weigh-In
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The night before states, Theo finds the original cassette Mrs. Ellery gave them tucked in his gym bag — Juniper returning it, a final kindness. Theo realizes Juniper kept it safe all along. Beat: clarity; Theo understands what choosing costs, and what not choosing costs more.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. During the championship, Juniper takes over the school radio station's open slot and plays Side B live, then speaks: his name, Danny's name, the truth, on air, to all nine hundred. In the gym, mid-match, Theo hears his own name in Juniper's mouth. Beat: climax — visibility chosen at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Forfeiture
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo walks off the mat in the third period, forfeiting the state title, and crosses the gym floor to the broadcast booth in front of everyone. His father leaves without him. Beat: the sacrifice that proves the choice; losing the championship that didn't matter.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The fallout: teammates divided, Mrs. Brandt quietly leaving a casserole, half the town furious and a surprising handful grateful. Juniper and Theo rebuild slowly, dating in daylight for the first time. Beat: bruised, imperfect hope; belonging redefined rather than granted.

chapters.title: A Mixtape for the Semester
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Graduation day. They submit the finished oral history — including the 1989 photo, names restored by Mrs. Ellery — and hand Ms. Voss the completed mixtape, both sides full. Final image: the two of them driving out of town with the windows down, the tape playing loud enough for anyone to hear. Beat: resolution — the song continues past the last track.
